text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "Terrorists" kill 27 people, including 12 women, in a raid in Benia village in Medea province, 70 km (45 miles) south of Algiers. The massacre was preceded by an attack earlier in the week on another hamlet, Ouzera, in Medea when 18 villagers were slaughtered by "terrorists". A bomb exploded in Ouzera cemetery where the 18 had been buried, killing three boy scouts.

- "Terrorists" cut the throats of three soccer fans caught at fake roadblock near Jenane Hassan on the northern part of the capital. The three young men were among tens of thousands of people who took to Algiers streets to celebrate Union Algiers soccer team who won the country's premier football cup on Saturday.

- Algiers's criminal court sentenced outlawed Islamic Salvation Front official Abdelkader Hachani to five years in jail. The court acquitted three journalists tried along with him on charges of printing a statement signed by Hachani calling on the military to disobey their leadership on cracking down on Moslem militants.
- Bank and insurance employees, who threatened to strike on Tuesday over pay increases, reach a deal on wage hike with employers.
